title: Force and torque conditions for equilibrium mark scheme

questions.answer: For a body in rotational equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about the same point.
accepted_alternatives: An equivalent statement using total clockwise moment equals total anticlockwise moment, with rotational equilibrium and the same point stated.

marking_points.text: States that the body is in rotational equilibrium.
States that the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about the same point.

option_feedback.A: Correct. Both the translational and rotational conditions are satisfied.
option_feedback.B: Zero speed is not an equilibrium condition. A body can be momentarily stationary while accelerating or rotating.
option_feedback.C: A non-zero resultant torque causes angular acceleration, so the body is not in equilibrium.
option_feedback.D: One clockwise sum and one force component do not establish zero resultant torque and zero resultant force in every direction.

marking_points.text: Selects A: resultant force is zero and resultant torque is zero.

option_feedback.A: Instantaneous zero speed does not imply zero acceleration or zero resultant force.
option_feedback.B: A zero torque condition would not remove the non-zero downward resultant force.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Weight acts downward with no balancing force, so the resultant force is non-zero.
option_feedback.D: Weight is vertical, not horizontal. The stated direction of the resultant force is wrong.

marking_points.text: Selects C: the ball is not in equilibrium because weight gives a non-zero resultant force.

option_feedback.A: The forces cancel translationally but their separated lines of action give a non-zero torque.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The resultant force is zero, while both forces turn the bar in the same sense.
option_feedback.C: The equal opposite forces give zero resultant force, so there is no linear acceleration.
option_feedback.D: Equal magnitudes do not prevent rotation when the lines of action are separated.

marking_points.text: Selects B: the bar has no linear acceleration but has angular acceleration.

parts.unit_policy: A unit is required for the final value; accept 7.56 kN with correct conversion.

marking_points.text: Uses vertical force balance as T - 7200 - 360 = 0, or an equivalent equation.
Calculates the upward cable tension as 7560 N.

parts.answer: The constant velocity means zero acceleration, and the calculated tension balances weight plus resistance, so the resultant force is zero. All forces share one line of action through the centre, so each has zero moment about the centre and the resultant torque is zero. Both conditions are met.
accepted_alternatives: Equivalent reasoning that establishes both zero resultant force and zero resultant torque.

marking_points.text: Links constant velocity or the balanced vertical forces to zero resultant force.
Uses the common line of action through the centre to establish zero resultant torque and concludes that both equilibrium conditions hold.

parts.answer: About A, the cable gives 48 x 0.90 = 43.2 N m anticlockwise and the lamp gives 72 x 0.60 = 43.2 N m clockwise. The moments are equal, so the resultant torque is zero.
accepted_alternatives: A correct comparison of the two 43.2 N m moments with their opposite senses.
parts.unit_policy: Moment values should include N m; accept a complete equality with correct force and distance even if the unit is stated once.

marking_points.text: Calculates the cable's anticlockwise moment about A as 48 x 0.90 = 43.2 N m.
Calculates the lamp's clockwise moment as 72 x 0.60 = 43.2 N m and concludes that the resultant torque is zero.
